provisions.title: Alabama Genetic Data Privacy Act: consumer consent requirements
provisions.quote: A genetic testing company shall obtain the consumer’s express consent every time the company does any of the following:
provisions.appliesTo: Any person, other than a health care provider, who directly solicits a biological sample from a consumer for analysis in order to provide products or services to the consumer

provisions.title: Alabama Genetic Data Privacy Act: exclusion of HIPAA entities
provisions.quote: A covered entity or business associate as those terms are defined in 45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164.
provisions.appliesTo: Lists entities to which the chapter does not apply.

provisions.title: Alabama Personal Data Protection Act: consent for sensitive data
provisions.quote: Process sensitive data concerning a consumer other than a known child without obtaining that consumer’s consent
provisions.appliesTo: Control or process the personal data of more than 25,000 consumers, excluding personal data controlled or processed solely for the purpose of completing a payment transaction.

leads.usedFor: Finding the 2024 genetic data privacy act

consumer_health_data.note: Act 2024-384 requires express consent from direct-to-consumer genetic testing companies, one class of non-HIPAA holder. Act 2026-552 requires consent for sensitive data, including health conditions, from May 1, 2027. Act 2026-552 § 12 sets that date.

crossCheck.note: Act 2024-384 section 7 sets October 1, 2024, read in HB21 enrolled text. It requires consent from one class of non-HIPAA holder, which gives level 2. Act 2026-552 (HB351) section 12 sets May 1, 2027, so pending is true.

freeCopyCases: When a physician leaves a group practice and the group notifies patients, the group bears the cost of reproducing or transferring records; if the departing physician notifies, the physician bears it (Ala. Admin. Code r. 540-X-9-.10).
feeRules: Ala. Code § 12-21-6.1(b)(2): "shall not be more than one dollar ($1) for each page of the first 25 pages, not more than 50 cents ($.50) for each page in excess of 25 pages, and a search fee of five dollars ($5)." Mailing at actual cost; X-rays at actual cost. Binds any medical provider or entity that maintains medical records.
Ala. Admin. Code r. 540-X-9-.10(b): "The cost of reproduction shall not exceed what is authorized under state and federal law." Binds physicians.

provisions.title: Joint Rules of the State Board of Medical Examiners and Medical Licensure Commission for Medical Records Management
provisions.quote: Absent a contractual provision to the contrary, when the group or medical practice undertakes to notify patients of the physician's departure, the group shall bear the cost of notifying patients and reproducing or transferring medical records.
provisions.appliesTo: Physicians and physician group practices licensed in Alabama; applies when a physician departs a group.

provisions.title: Reproduction and Delivery of Medical Records
provisions.quote: shall not be more than one dollar ($1) for each page of the first 25 pages, not more than 50 cents ($.50) for each page in excess of 25 pages, and a search fee of five dollars ($5).
provisions.appliesTo: Any medical provider or company or other legal entity that maintains medical records.

leads.usedFor: Finding the medical records management rule
Finding the medical records management rule

copy_rights.note: No state deadline found. Free case is narrow: records transfer when a physician leaves a group, cost on the practice or physician. HIPAA permits a fee for such copies, so this goes beyond the federal floor. Per-page cap is a fact only.

crossCheck.note: beyondFederalFloor yes: the rule puts the cost of copying or transferring records on the practice or departing physician, covering paper copies, so it is more than free electronic self-access. No deadline under 30 days found in code search.

hie_consent.designatedHie: Alabama One Health Record (statewide HIE administered by the Alabama Medicaid Agency)

provisions.title: Alabama Health Information Exchange Policy Manual, AHIE Policy 006, Individual Participation and Choice (Opt-Out Procedures)
provisions.quote: the Participant shall provide Individuals the option to choose not to participate in the electronic sharing of his or her protected health information through One Health Record
provisions.appliesTo: All participants in One Health Record. Same manual: exchange for permitted purposes needs no authorization, and data is available unless the person has opted out. Manual states One Health Record is administered and managed by the Alabama Medicaid Agency. Live file sits behind a captcha; stored bytes are the Wayback Machine raw capture of 2026-05-14.

provisions.title: Alabama One Health Record Patient Opt-Out Info and Request to Opt-Out/Reverse Opt-Out form

provisions.quote: Your choice to opt-out of the health information exchange will not affect your ability to access medical care.
provisions.appliesTo: Patients of providers participating in One Health Record; the signed form goes to a participating provider. Effective date taken from the form version string v2.071521. Stored bytes are the Wayback Machine raw capture of 2026-05-14 (live site captcha).

provisions.title: Alabama One Health Record FAQs, What if patients do not want their information shared?
provisions.quote: Opt-Out assistance is also available through our Service Desk at 844-746-3540.
provisions.appliesTo: Patients; page undated. Stored bytes are the Wayback Machine raw capture of 2026-05-14 (live site captcha).

provisions.title: Alabama Medicaid Agency, Accessing Your Health Information
provisions.citation: Alabama Medicaid Agency patient access page
provisions.quote: Alabama Medicaid offers the Alabama One Health Record App
provisions.appliesTo: State agency page that names One Health Record and links to it as "One Health Record - HIE"; used for the exchange name, not the consent rule.

leads.usedFor: Medicaid news item dated 5/28/2015 calls One Health Record Alabama's HIE and says providers must offer an opt-out; history only
Hospital copy of the HIE opt-out form

hie_consent.note: No Alabama statute on HIE consent was found (earlier code search). One Health Record, run by the Alabama Medicaid Agency, publishes an opt-out policy (Policy 006, effective 1 October 2023) and a patient opt-out form. The live exchange site returns a DataDome captcha, so the stored copies are raw Wayback Machine captures of the official files from 14 May 2026. The policy manual defers to law for sensitive information and sets no added consent step of its own.

provisions.title: Reports of Induced Termination of Pregnancy
provisions.quote: Individual induced termination of pregnancy reports shall be maintained in strict confidence by the Office of Vital Statistics, shall not be available for public inspection, and shall not be made available except:
provisions.appliesTo: Reports filed with the Office of Vital Statistics; exceptions include the Attorney General or a district attorney in a criminal investigation.

reproductive.note: Rule covers state vital statistics reports of induced termination of pregnancy, not provider records generally. Listed exceptions allow release to prosecutors and by court order. Act 2012-363 took effect on approval.

crossCheck.note: Latest amendment is Act 2012-363 (HB362), approved 5-14-2012 per Secretary of State. Its section 7 makes it effective on approval. Subdivision (b)(5) text dates from Act 2011-672.

provisions.title: Data Breach Notification Act: violations
provisions.quote: A violation of this chapter does not establish a private cause of action under Section 8-19-10.
provisions.appliesTo: Covered entities and third-party agents under the breach chapter.

provisions.title: Alabama Genetic Data Privacy Act: enforcement
provisions.quote: may enforce this chapter by a civil action in circuit court to enjoin any practice or conduct in violation of this chapter or to recover a civil penalty of up to three thousand dollars ($3,000) for each violation.
provisions.appliesTo: Consumer Interest Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

provisions.title: Alabama Personal Data Protection Act: enforcement
provisions.quote: The Attorney General may enforce violations of this chapter.
provisions.appliesTo: Controllers and processors meeting the § 8-44-3 thresholds.

private_right.note: Breach act bars a private action under § 8-19-10. Genetic act and the 2027 privacy act are enforced by the Attorney General only. No health records statute found that lets a person sue.

crossCheck.note: My code searches found no health records cause of action. Section 22-56-4(b)(14) gives mental health consumers a court enforcement right, but 22-56-10 bars expanding rights beyond other persons. Flag for review; level 0 kept.

provisions.title: Data Breach Notification Act: definitions (medical information)
provisions.quote: Any information regarding an individual’s medical history, mental or physical condition, or medical treatment or diagnosis by a health care professional.
provisions.appliesTo: Covered entities: any person or business or government entity that acquires or uses sensitive personally identifying information.

provisions.title: Data Breach Notification Act: definitions (health insurance information)
provisions.quote: An individual’s health insurance policy number or subscriber identification number and any unique identifier used by a health insurer to identify the individual.
provisions.appliesTo: Covered entities under the breach chapter.

provisions.title: Notice of Security Breach: Individuals Affected
provisions.quote: the covered entity shall provide notice within 45 days of the covered entity’s receipt of notice from a third-party agent that a breach has occurred
provisions.appliesTo: Breaches reasonably likely to cause substantial harm.

provisions.title: Notice of Security Breach: Attorney General
provisions.quote: If the number of individuals a covered entity is required to notify under Section 8-38-5 exceeds 1,000, the entity shall provide written notice of the breach to the Attorney General as expeditiously as possible and without unreasonable delay.
provisions.appliesTo: Breaches requiring notice to more than 1,000 individuals.

provisions.title: Exemptions: Federal
provisions.quote: is exempt from this chapter as long as the entity does all of the following:
provisions.appliesTo: Entities subject to federal breach notification rules that keep procedures, notify individuals under those rules, and copy the Attorney General when over 1,000 are notified.

breach_health.note: Act 2018-396 § 13 sets effect on the first day of the third month after approval (approved March 28, 2018), so June 1, 2018. Both medical and health insurance information are in the definition.

crossCheck.note: Legislature's 2018 summaries list Act 2018-396 effective June 1, 2018. Notice within 45 days. Attorney General notice when over 1,000. Section 8-38-11 exempts entities that follow federal breach rules.
